# Automated checks

Machines enforce these in CI; keep them green, and never silence one to get green. Fix the new finding; a baseline only shrinks.

- **PHP quality floor:** PHPStan (Larastan) at level **8** at least in apps and **`max`** in packages; the level never drops and `phpstan-baseline.neon` only shrinks. Apps run Pest with line coverage in CI and fail below the committed `coverage-floor.txt`, which only rises; packages keep a fixed minimum per path. Both run in the reusable `php-quality.yml`.

- **Dead code.** `knip` (unused files, exports, dependencies) runs in CI with the repo's committed `knip.json`. TypeScript has `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` on. Delete what is unused; prefix a parameter a signature forces on you with `_`. A knip `ignore*` entry needs a comment-worthy reason in the PR.
- **Strict models.** Each app's `AppServiceProvider::boot()` calls `Model::shouldBeStrict(! app()->isProduction())`: lazy loading, silently discarded attributes and missing attributes throw outside production. Fix the query (eager load, `$fillable`, select the column), never turn it off.
- **PHPStan level floor and baseline ratchet.** Apps run Larastan at level 8 or above, packages at `max`. `scripts/qiick-ratchet.mjs phpstan --min-level 8` (`max` in packages) fails CI when `level:` is below the floor or lower than on the base branch, and when `phpstan-baseline.neon` holds more errors than on the base branch. Only the PR that raises `level:` may baseline that level's errors, once. Never add to the baseline; fix the new error. An app below the floor (externa-core at 6) raises the level one step per PR, paying the baseline down in between, and calls `php-quality.yml` with `phpstan-min-level: ''` until it reaches 8.
- **Coverage ratchet.** Pest runs with line coverage (pcov) and writes a Clover report; `scripts/qiick-ratchet.mjs coverage --clover <report>` counts its statement lines.
    - **Apps:** the total must reach the floor committed in `coverage-floor.txt` (one number, a percentage). The floor only rises: CI fails when a PR lowers it below the base branch. When coverage passes the floor by a point or more, the job says so; raise the floor in that PR with `--update`, which writes the current total rounded down.
    - **Packages:** a fixed minimum per path, `<path>=<percent>` (excubia-core: `src=90 src/Checks=90`); a path counts the files under it, and a path with no PHP file yet is skipped.
- **One reusable job.** `qiick-io/app-ui/.github/workflows/php-quality.yml` runs PHPStan, the level floor, the baseline ratchet, Pest with coverage and the coverage ratchet with the repo's synced `scripts/qiick-ratchet.mjs` (check `php-quality / php-quality`). Apps call it instead of copying those steps; packages pass `phpstan-min-level: max`, `coverage-thresholds` and `build-command: ''`.
- **Theme tokens only.** In apps with the qiick UI, `scripts/check-ui-tokens.mjs` (synced by the pack, part of `npm run lint`) fails on arbitrary font sizes (`text-[11px]`) and on raw palette / `#hex` classes beyond `scripts/ui-token-baseline.txt`; the baseline only shrinks. The reusable `ui-quality.yml` runs it with the WCAG 2.2 AA contrast check of the installed theme and the app's axe smoke browser test (light, dark, high contrast).
- **Ratcheted code rules.** In Vite+ apps the synced `.oxlintrc.standards.json` runs them in Oxlint (`npm run lint:standards`, `--rule eslint/<rule>`); in repos still on ESLint, `qiickRatchetedRules()` from `qiick-standards.eslint.js` does. They turn prose rules into checks: only `lucide-react` icons and shadcn primitives (`no-restricted-imports` on other icon and component libraries), toasts only through `@/lib/toast` (not `sonner`), the clipboard only through `@/lib/clipboard` (`no-restricted-properties` on `navigator.clipboard`), booleans prefixed `is` / `has` / `can` / `should` (`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`, type-aware; destructured contract names exempt), no single-letter names (`id-length`; `i`, `j`, `k`, `t`, `_` allowed), files and functions within the size tripwire (`max-lines` 600, `max-lines-per-function` 300, lines of code; generated Wayfinder output and `components/ui` excluded; see the code standard, Size). They run only in `npm run lint:standards` (`QIICK_RATCHET=1`), ratcheted per file and rule against `qiick-lint-baseline.json`: existing debt is listed, new findings fail, paid debt must be removed (`--update`). A rule missing from the script's `--rule` list is not checked at all: when the pack adds a rule, every app adds it to `lint:standards` and seeds it with `--update`.
- **Registry coverage.** The drift check (`app-ui-drift / drift`, `scripts/check-drift.mjs`) compares every file of the registry items an app installed with the registry, and fails on a difference that `app-ui.overrides.json` does not explain. That proves the fidelity of what an app took and nothing about what it never took: four API key screens grew under a green check because none of them was an installed item. So the app also lists in `qiick-standards.json` the items its product must install (`requiredItems`), and each one it leaves out on purpose under `divergences` with the reason, the overrides idea one level up: `"divergences": { "api-key-form": "Keys are issued per tenant; the shared form has no tenant picker (#171)" }`. The check fails on a required item that is neither installed nor declared, and on a divergence whose item is installed (a stale exception: remove it; a file that differs belongs in the overrides), is not required, or has no reason. Divergence stays allowed; it has to be written down. Which items a product requires is the maintainer's decision; until it is made, the list is empty.
- **Thin controllers.** The architecture test fails on a controller with more than five public methods of its own; controllers that already have more are listed with their count in `tests/Arch/naming-architecture.php` (`controllerPublicMethods`), and the test fails when a count grows or when it shrinks without the entry being lowered.
- **Legacy web platform patterns (ratchet).** `scripts/check-legacy-web.mjs` runs Google Chrome's `legacy-scan` (`modern-web-guidance`, Apache-2.0, no dependencies) over the repo's frontend roots and ratchets it against `legacy-scan-baseline.json`. The scanner always exits 0, findings or not, so the script is the gate: it fails on a finding in a file the baseline does not list for that rule, on one more finding than it allows, and when a fixed finding is still allowed (lower it with `--update`, so paid debt cannot come back). Findings are keyed by **rule and file, never by line**, so an edit above a finding does not churn the baseline while a new file and a new rule are still caught. The scanner version is pinned in the script and recorded in each baseline; never `@latest`, which would turn every repo red the day Chrome adds a rule. Bumping the pin is its own PR: change it in the pack, sync, re-run with `--update` and review the new findings there. The findings are provisional (deterministic rules for 38 of about 200 guides, a fifth of the corpus), so read the guide with `npx modern-web-guidance retrieve <guideId>` and check the finding against its Keep/Drop criteria before fixing it. It runs as a step in the repo's existing lint job, never a job of its own.
- **No hard-coded UI strings.** `i18next/no-literal-string` (JSX text only, not attributes such as `className` or `data-*`) flags visible text that bypasses translations: use `t('…')` with keys in every locale file. Existing debt is in `i18n-literal-baseline.json`; `scripts/qiick-ratchet.mjs lint` fails when a file's count grows, and when a count shrinks without the baseline being lowered (`--update`).
- **graphify stays local.** The standards check (`app-ui-drift / standards`, `scripts/sync-standards.mjs --check`) fails when `.gitignore` does not ignore `graphify-out/`, when any `graphify-out/` path is tracked, or when `.gitattributes` contains `merge=graphify` (that line comes from `graphify hook install` and must stay uncommitted). Rebuild the graph locally; never commit it.

## CI cost

**GitHub bills per job, rounded up to the whole minute.** A job that runs for ten seconds costs a minute, so a seven-job workflow costs seven minutes however fast it is, and a workflow that runs twice per commit costs twice that. Measured on externa-core, one push cost ~95 billable minutes. Every rule below follows from that one fact: minutes are paid, and CI that burns them gets switched off, which blocks every repo behind it.

- **`push` only on `main` and `develop`.** Everything else arrives through `pull_request`. Without the branch filter, pushing to a branch that already has an open pull request runs every workflow twice on the same commit: twice the bill, no extra signal.

    ```yaml
    on:
        push:
            branches: [main, develop]
        pull_request:
    ```

- **`concurrency` on every workflow, with the event in the group.** A superseded run keeps paying until it finishes, so three pushes in a row cost three full runs. Keep `github.event_name` in the group: a group of `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` alone does not distinguish the events, so the `push` run and the `pull_request` run on the same commit cancel each other and the cancelled required check never reports (externa-core#805). Never cancel in progress on `main` or `develop`: those runs are the release evidence.

    ```yaml
    concurrency:
        group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}
        cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' && github.ref != 'refs/heads/develop' }}
    ```

    **`concurrency` inside a reusable workflow does not govern the caller's run**, and the caller is where the duplicate runs come from: a `concurrency:` block in a `workflow_call` workflow cannot cancel the run that called it. This is the mistake everyone makes. The shared workflows in this repo therefore set none, and every repo that calls them sets `concurrency` in its own calling workflow.

- **arm64 / QEMU builds only on a release.** Cross-architecture builds run under emulation and cost an order of magnitude more than the native one (externa-core: `multiarch-bake` alone is 39 of those 95 minutes). Build `linux/amd64` on every push, and the full `linux/amd64,linux/arm64` manifest only when the pull request targets `main`, the ref is a `v*` tag, or on `workflow_dispatch`. The amd64 job keeps its name and keeps running on every push: it is a required check in some repos (`image-build` on externa-core, `Docker image` on excubia-app).

- **Never `paths:` or `paths-ignore:` on a workflow that produces a required check.** A required check that never runs stays _pending forever_ and the pull request can never be merged: there is no timeout and no way out short of the maintainer editing branch protection by hand. Skip the work inside the workflow instead: a tiny `changes` job that always runs and classifies the diff, and every heavy job gated on `if: needs.changes.outputs.<area> == 'true'` while still reporting. A required check that must be skipped still has to report success, so use a guard job with the same name, never a skipped job. When in doubt leave the heavy job running: a blocked `main` costs more than the minutes.

- **Never buy minutes with a check name.** Merging small jobs into one saves a minute each, and renames the checks. A required check whose name no workflow reports any more blocks every pull request until the maintainer edits branch protection, so the saving is never an agent's to take: propose it, name the old and new check names, and wait (`rules/release.md`, "Required checks per repo").
